newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RW RICK TOCCHET SIGNS THREE-YEAR DEAL WITH PHOENIX.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RW RICK TOCCHET SIGNS THREE-YEAR DEAL WITH PHOENIX.

text.p: The Phoenix Coyotes added veteran right wing Rick Tocchet to their lineup Tuesday, signing him to a three-year-contract.
The 33-year-old four-time NHL All-Star, who was an unrestricted free agent, is known for both toughness and scoring ability.

"I am pleased to add a player of Rich Tocchet's character and ability," said Coyotes general manager Bobby Smith. "He is a legitimate front-line player who will have an immediate impact on our record."
It is believed the Coyotes will use Tocchet on a line with budding superstar left wing Keith Tkachuk, a pairing that could give new life to Tocchet's career.
"I am excited to be a part of a new franchise in a new hockey town," Tocchet said. "Since the first day, the Coyotes have shown a committment to winning, and I hope to help them achieve their goal."
In Phoenix, Tocchet will be reunited with coach Jim Schoenfeld, who was briefly his coach in Washington last season and was hired by the Coyotes in the off-season.
Tocchet was traded to the Washington Capitals with centre Adam Oates and goaltender Bill Ranford by the Boston Bruins in a major deal at the trade deadline last season.
Tocchet decided not re-sign with Washington after general manager David Poile's contract was not renewed and Schoenfeld was fired. George McPhee is the new Capitals GM and Ron Wilson the new coach.
Tocchet, who has nine 20-goal seasons in his 13-year career, joins Dale Hunter, Pat Verbeek and Mike Foligno as the only players in NHL history with 300 career goals and 2,000 penalty minutes.

He began his career with the Philadelphia Flyers, for whom he had two 40-goal seasons. In seven-plus seasons with the Flyers, Tocchet made the All-Star team three times and scored the game-winning goal in the 1987 Wales Conference finals against the Montreal Canadiens to send Philadelphia into the Stanley Cup Finals.
Tocchet also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins team that won the 1992 Stanley Cup.
